title: Of the Appointed Term

full_text:
On the tenth and final day, the Tenth Wazir demanded that the execution proceed without delay. Bakhtiyar stepped forward and delivered his final, crowning discourse before King Azadbakht:

'O King! Every mortal creature has an appointed term upon this earth. The mightiest conqueror whose armies shook the continents, and the humble beggar who slept upon the doorstep, both step down into the same narrow earthen bed.

Neither gold, nor ivory palaces, nor armies of iron can delay the hour by a single heartbeat.

What then remains of a king when his body is laid beneath the marble?

His gold is plundered by strangers, his palaces crumble into dust, and his armies are scattered by time. Only one treasure outlasts the grave: the memory of the tears he wiped away, the justice he established, the schools he built, and the mercy he showed to the weak!

He who lives for his own selfish vanity dies completely; but he who lives for the welfare of his fellow men achieves an immortality that shines brighter than the stars, as the chronicle of King Sulayman Shah demonstrates.'
moral: Earthly life is a passing journey; only the enduring memory of justice and charity outlives the grave.
